summary: THE PATTERN IS MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES OF THE JOINT. Servo side: cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders on xl330.stl reads Ø16.0 x 3.0 bosses on both faces (centres x ±13.0) and 8 x Ø1.6 x 6.0 holes at (y,z) = (0,±6),(±6,0) — a Ø12.0 bolt circle, Ø1.6 being the cecad fasteners.py M2 tap drill; frozen in the artifact. Bracket side: 10+ microduck ce-parts interfaces with role horn_face carry the mirror pattern with their own measured numbers — shin knee 4 x Ø2.2 on an 8.486 square (diagonal 8.486 x sqrt2 = 12.001, agreeing with the Ø12 PCD to 0.001 mm), yaw2roll 4 x Ø2.2 on r 6.0, hip-bracket Ø2.4 on Ø12 with Ø4.84 cbores. compat.py graded the shin pair live: bolt_circle PASS at delta 0.001 mm.
by: claude (microduck connections lane), meshfeatures + interface scan

summary: NO PUBLISHED STANDARD DEFINES THE XL330 HORN PATTERN — it is ROBOTIS's own, so record.standard is null and T4 is structurally out of reach for this folder; that is correct, not a gap to fill. The pattern facts rest on the mesh measurement (previous row) and on ce-parts/xl330-m288-t, whose vendor drawing 'XL,XC-330.pdf' is fetched and hashed in that folder's PROVENANCE.json; reading the horn hub diameter off that drawing is the named way to close the centre-pilot unknown.

THREE THINGS STAY OPEN AND EACH NAMES ITS CLOSER. (1) Horn centre hub: xl330.stl has NO centre feature (cecad.meshslice axis probe solid -14.5..14.5, in the artifact of the pattern row) while every bracket carries a Ø5-6 centre bore — the decimated mesh hid the hub; the ROBOTIS horn drawing would settle it. (2) Clamp/strip torque of 4 M2s in tapped plastic: nothing twisted off with a gauge here; the vendor 0.52 N.m stall (ce-parts/xl330-m288-t) is the load to beat, not evidence. (3) Output-spline clocking: the internal spline is not in the mesh; mate() carries clock_deg verbatim as a build decision.
